title: The Foolish Weaver (தமிழ்)

full_text:
In a quiet village near Isfahan lived an honest weaver who produced durable linen cloth for coats and sails. Though his trade did not make him wealthy, it provided warm bread, honey, and olive oil for his family, and his neighbors respected him for his even stitching.

One spring morning, a traveling troupe of acrobats arrived in the village square. The crowd gathered with breathless excitement as a master rope-dancer climbed a high mast, balanced upon a slender rope stretched between two minarets, leaped into the air, and landed with supreme grace upon his toes. The spectators threw handfuls of silver coins, cheering the acrobat's daring skill.

The weaver watched with wide eyes, his heart consumed by sudden envy. 'What a fool I am!' he thought bitterly. 'I sit hunched over a wooden loom all day long, throwing a wooden shuttle back and forth for a few miserable copper pennies, while this man dances in the air for ten minutes and fills his purse with silver dinars! Tomorrow, I too shall become a famous rope-dancer!'

He returned home, kicked his loom into the corner, and refused to weave another thread. Climbing up to the flat roof of his house, he tied a slender clothesline between two tall chimney pots. Without practicing, without testing the rope, and without taking off his heavy wooden clogs, the foolish weaver stepped boldly onto the slender cord!

The moment his full weight pressed upon the rope, the line snapped like dry grass. The weaver tumbled head over heels from the roof, crashed through his neighbor’s wicker chicken coop, and landed flat on his back in a trough of muddy ditch-water, spraining both his wrists and bruising his ribs.

His wife and neighbors ran out with smelling salts and pulled him from the mud. As the village bonesetter bandaged his fractured wrists, the weaver groaned in agony: 'Cursed be the pride that made me despise my shuttle! The loom was built for my hands, but the sky was meant for eagles and acrobats.' He returned to his loom the moment his bones healed, never again casting envious eyes upon the feats of others.
moral: Do not abandon your proven skill to pursue flashy accomplishments for which you possess neither training nor talent. [TA]
